adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:23 — WorkItem.message field is stored but never read anywhere after construction, adding an unused coupling to the raw Kafka Message/KafkaPayload type

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, WorkItem includes a `message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]` field (used when constructing `WorkItem` in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`), but the worker/queue logic only ever reads `work_item.result`, `partition`, and `offset` (e.g., `OrderedQueueWorker.run` and `OffsetTracker.complete_offset`). There are no reads of `work_item.message` anywhere in the diff, including tests, so this field currently adds an unnecessary coupling to raw Kafka/Arroyo message types without providing functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:222 — FixedQueuePool.wait_until_empty is defined but never called from any production code path (only test-relevant), appears dead code

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, FixedQueuePool defines wait_until_empty(timeout=5.0), but within the diff there are no production-call sites for it: ResultsStrategyFactory only uses FixedQueuePool via submit/get_stats/shutdown (e.g., SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.poll() calls get_stats; close/terminate call shutdown). The added tests also do not call wait_until_empty. This makes the method appear unused/dead code in the context of this PR, which is a maintainability concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py:99 — queue_pool: FixedQueuePool | None omits the generic type parameter (FixedQueuePool[T]), losing type-checking on submit/result_processor consistency

adjudication.rationale: In `ResultsStrategyFactory` (a `Generic[T, ...]`), the diff adds `queue_pool: FixedQueuePool | None = None` without parameterizing it as `FixedQueuePool[T]`. This is verifiable in the diff and would reduce mypy/typing’s ability to enforce consistency between `decoder`/`grouping_fn` output type `T` and what `FixedQueuePool`/`SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` expect, but it does not introduce a runtime correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:130 — get_queue_for_group uses hash(group_key) % self.num_queues, which is not stable across process restarts if group_key hashing relies on Python's randomized str hashing (PYTHONHASHSEED), risking inconsistent ordering assumptions across runs though not within a single process

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `FixedQueuePool.get_queue_for_group` implemented as `return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues`, and Python’s built-in `hash(str)` is typically randomized between interpreter runs (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the queue assignment for a given `group_key` can change across process restarts. However, the ordering guarantee described/implemented is within a single running consumer process (one queue per worker thread, FIFO), and a restart resets all in-memory queues/workers anyway, so this doesn’t create an in-process ordering bug or offset-commit correctness issue by itself. It is still a legitimate design concern if “consistent hashing” across restarts or predictable queue affinity was intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:174 — queue.Queue() in FixedQueuePool.__init__ has no maxsize, so submit() never blocks and a slow/stuck worker on one hashed queue lets that queue grow unbounded with no backpressure to the Kafka consumer

adjudication.rationale: In `FixedQueuePool.__init__`, each worker queue is created as `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize` (unbounded). In `FixedQueuePool.submit`, it calls `work_queue.put(work_item)` which will not block on an unbounded queue, so the processing strategy will continue accepting messages even if a particular hashed queue’s worker is slow/stuck, allowing unbounded in-memory growth. This also contradicts the stated guarantee in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` docstring: “Natural backpressure when queues fill up.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:220 — get_queue_for_group uses hash(group_key) % num_queues with no throughput awareness, so a single hot group can overload one queue/worker while others sit idle, effectively capping overall throughput to one thread's capacity

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly implements `FixedQueuePool.get_queue_for_group` as `hash(group_key) % self.num_queues`, and each queue has exactly one worker thread (`OrderedQueueWorker`). This design guarantees per-group ordering but also means a single “hot” group will always be routed to the same single queue/worker, which can become a throughput bottleneck while other workers are idle. That is a real performance/architecture limitation introduced by this change, not a correctness defect per se.
